summary: Second run today. Proposing 4 official additions for the build-and-test loop: Playwright MCP, Anthropic's frontend-design skill, and the Pyright and TypeScript LSP plugins for Claude Code. No upstream updates to pinned items.

candidates.name: frontend-design
candidates.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional UI design.
candidates.reason: Official, instruction-only; covers frontend design, which nothing installed does.

candidates.name: pyright-lsp
candidates.description: Pyright language server for Claude Code.
candidates.reason: Official manifest-only plugin; live type checking for the Python stack. Needs pyright installed.

candidates.name: playwright
candidates.description: Browser automation and end-to-end testing MCP server.
candidates.reason: Official Microsoft, in the MCP registry; a live browser in every harness, pinned to 0.0.85.

candidates.name: typescript-lsp
candidates.description: TypeScript/JavaScript language server for Claude Code.
candidates.reason: Official manifest-only plugin; diagnostics for the generated TypeScript. Needs typescript-language-server installed.

candidates.name: claude-api
candidates.reason: Claude Code already bundles it and keeps it current with model releases; a pinned copy would carry outdated model IDs. Revisit if Codex or Cursor needs it.

candidates.name: serena
candidates.description: Semantic code retrieval and editing over LSP via MCP.
candidates.reason: Custom license; overlaps GitNexus plus the proposed LSP plugins. Reconsider if those fall short.

candidates.name: elephant-goldfish-model
candidates.description: Spec drafting with fresh-context reviewer agents.
candidates.reason: Official Google, Apache-2.0; overlaps writing-plans and grilling. Worth a trial for design reviews.

candidates.name: context-mode
candidates.description: Keeps tool output out of the context window via a local sandbox and SQLite index.
candidates.reason: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available) and hooks every tool call; promising for context budgets, but review the hooks first.

candidates.name: open-code-review
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0; overlaps the built-in /code-review and the superpowers review skills.

candidates.name: ghidra-mcp
candidates.reason: REA already drives Ghidra; only worth it for deep Ghidra-only work.

candidates.name: Understand-Anything
candidates.reason: Third code-graph tool after GitNexus and graphify (watch); README promotes an unrelated commercial agent.

candidates.name: planning-with-files
candidates.description: File-based planning enforced by a per-turn hook.
candidates.reason: Overlaps writing-plans/executing-plans and adds a hook that fires every turn.

candidates.name: academy-guide / discernment-nudge
candidates.description: Claude Academy recommendations; nudges after substantive answers.
candidates.reason: Product-education nudges, not developer tools; would add noise to coding sessions.

candidates.name: graphify
candidates.description: Codebase + docs + schemas into a queryable graph.
candidates.reason: Apache-2.0 code knowledge graph (147k stars). Strong alternative to GitNexus, whose PolyForm Noncommercial license rules out work use. Compare on your monorepos before switching.

candidates.name: codebase-memory-mcp
candidates.reason: MIT code-intelligence graph; overlaps GitNexus. Keep as a fallback.

candidates.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
candidates.reason: Official Chrome DevTools MCP for frontend debugging; candidate for next run (overlaps webapp-testing).

candidates.name: github-mcp-server
candidates.reason: Official GitHub MCP; needs a PAT. gh CLI already covers most needs, so deferred.

candidates.name: ida-pro-mcp
candidates.reason: Popular IDA bridge; REA already wraps IDA/Ghidra/Hopper. Only worth it if you use IDA directly.

candidates.name: leanrea
candidates.reason: 8 KB CLI-only alternative to REA claiming lower cost; compare after you have used REA.

candidates.name: agent-skills
candidates.reason: Strong engineering skills; overlaps superpowers. Revisit after a week with superpowers.

candidates.name: context-engineering skills
candidates.description: Skills for context engineering and multi-agent design.
candidates.reason: Focused context-engineering collection (MIT, 1 curated list); review individual skills next run.

candidates.name: claude-mem
candidates.reason: Popular persistent-memory plugin; captures all sessions, so review privacy and storage first.

candidates.name: ECC
candidates.reason: Sprawling harness overlay (skills, hooks, memory, settings) that overlaps superpowers and rewrites a lot of config.

candidates.name: firecrawl
candidates.reason: AGPL and a hosted API key for web scraping; WebFetch covers current needs.

candidates.name: n8n
candidates.reason: A workflow platform, not a skill or MCP server.
